**findings** (noun): Small tools and materials used by artisans and craftsmen

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**resident** (noun): 1. A person, animal or plant living at a certain location or in a certain area. 2. A bird which does not migrate during the course of the year. 3. A physician receiving postgraduate medical training in a hospital or clinic.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**friend** (noun): 1. A person, typically someone other than a family member, spouse or lover, whose company one enjoys and towards whom one feels affection. 2. An associate who provides assistance; patron, mentor. 3. A person with whom one is vaguely or indirectly acquainted.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**front** (noun): 1. The foremost side of something or the end that faces the direction it normally moves. 2. The side of a building with the main entrance. 3. A field of activity.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**filmed** (verb): 1. Covered with a film. 2. Covered with a film of (a specified type or substance).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**goalless** (adjective): 1. Devoid of goals; ambitionless. 2. Without goals; in which no goals have been scored; having scored no goals.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**gameplay** (noun): The totality of player experiences during a game, such as the gaming environment and the competitive interaction with other players; often with reference to a video game or a board game.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**guard** (noun): 1. A person who, or thing that, protects or watches over something. 2. A garda; a police officer. 3. A squad responsible for protecting something.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**guy** (noun): 1. An effigy, properly of Guy Fawkes, to be burned on a bonfire on the anniversary of the Gunpowder Plot (5th November). 2. A person of eccentric appearance or dress; a "fright". 3. A man or boy; a fellow.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hall** (noun): 1. A corridor; a hallway. 2. A large meeting room. 3. A manor house (originally because a magistrate's court was held in the hall of his mansion).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**husband** (noun): 1. A man in a marriage or marital relationship, especially in relation to his spouse. 2. A manager of property; one who has the care of another's belongings, owndom, or interests; a steward; an economist. 3. A prudent or frugal manager.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**happy** (adjective): 1. Having a feeling arising from a consciousness of well-being or of enjoyment; enjoying good of any kind, such as comfort, peace, or tranquillity; blissful, contented, joyous. 2. Experiencing the effect of favourable fortune; favored by fortune or luck; fortunate, lucky. 3. Elect or saved after death, blessed.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**haven** (noun): 1. A harbour or anchorage protected from the sea. 2. A safe place. 3. A peaceful or tranquil place.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**happen** (verb): 1. To occur or take place. 2. To happen to; to befall. 3. To do or occur by chance or unexpectedly.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hack** (verb): 1. To chop or cut down in a rough manner. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. To withstand or put up with a difficult situation. 3. To make a quick code change to patch a computer program, often one that, while being effective, is inelegant or makes the program harder to maintain.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**heard** (verb): 1. That has been perceived aurally. 2. I understand; gotcha.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hubs** (noun): Husband.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**highly** (adverb): 1. In a high or esteemed manner. 2. Extremely; greatly; very much.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**human** (adjective): 1. Of or belonging to the species Homo sapiens or its closest relatives. 2. Having the nature or attributes of a human being. 3. Compassionate.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hippo** (noun): 1. Clipping of hippopotamus. 2. An armored personnel carrier used by the South African Defence Force. 3. An overweight or obese person.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hat** (noun): 1. A particular role or capacity that a person might fill. 2. Any receptacle from which names or numbers are pulled out in a lottery. The lottery or draw itself. 3. The lottery or draw itself.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**hour** (noun): 1. A unit of time of one twenty-fourth of a day (sixty minutes). 2. A season, moment, or time. 3. The time.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**inappropriate** (adjective): 1. Not appropriate; not suitable for the situation, time, or place. 2. Improper; adult; sexual. 3. (of an action or thing) vile or unpleasant; repulsive.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**iryo** (phrase): Initialism of I respect your opinion.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**inspired** (adjective): 1. Having excellence through inspiration. 2. Filled with inspiration or motivated. 3. Infused with power or knowledge granted from a supernatural entity; possessing inspiration from the divine.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**real-life** (adjective): 1. As happens in real life; not fictional or theoretical; actual as opposed to believed or assumed. 2. Not online, in real life.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**interim** (adjective): 1. transitional 2. temporary 3. A transitional or temporary period between other events.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**included** (verb): 1. Provided as an accompaniment or gratuity. 2. Enclosed, not protruding, e.g. stamens within the corolla.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**interested** (adjective): 1. Having or showing interest (attention or curiosity). 2. Having an interest (stake); being a stakeholder; motivated by considerations of self-interest; self-serving. 3. Owning a share of a company; being a shareholder.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**improved** (adjective): That has been made better; enhanced.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**intended** (adjective): 1. Planned. 2. Made tense; stretched out; extended; forcible; violent. 3. Fiancé or fiancée.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**prestigious** (adjective): Of high prestige.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**secret** (noun): 1. A piece of knowledge that is hidden and intended to be kept hidden. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. The key or principle by which something is made clear; the knack. 3. Something not understood or known.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**try** (verb): 1. To attempt; to endeavour. Followed by infinitive. 2. To divide; to separate. To separate (precious metal etc.) from the ore by melting; to purify, refine. To winnow; to sift; to pick out; frequently followed by out. 3. To separate (precious metal etc.) from the ore by melting; to purify, refine.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**went** (verb): A course; a way, a path; a journey.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**album** (noun): 1. In Ancient Rome, a white tablet or register on which the praetor's edicts and other public notices were recorded. 2. A book specially designed to keep photographs, stamps, or autographs. 3. A collection, especially of literary items.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**actress** (noun): 1. A female who performs on the stage or in films. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A female doer or "actor" (in a general sense).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**creating** (verb): creation

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**identity** (noun): 1. Sameness, identicalness; the quality or fact of (several specified things) being the same. 2. The difference or character that marks off an individual or collective from the rest of the same kind; selfhood; the sense of who something or someone or oneself is, or the recurring characteristics that enable the recognition of such an individual or group by others or themselves. 3. A name or persona—a mask or appearance one presents to the world—by which one is known.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**indicate** (verb): 1. To point out; to discover; to direct to a knowledge of; to show; to make known. 2. To show or manifest by symptoms. 3. To point to as the proper remedies.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**initiative** (adjective): 1. Serving to initiate. 2. In which voter initiatives can be brought to the ballot. 3. A beginning; a first move.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**internet** (proper noun): 1. Internet access or connection; internet connectivity. 2. Any set of computer networks that communicate using the Internet Protocol; an intranet. 3. A fictitious unit of scoring awarded for making outstanding posts on the internet.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**yuko** (noun): The score for a throw that lands the opponent on his or her side.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**joining** (verb): The act or result of joining; a joint or juncture.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**jail** (noun): 1. A place or institution for the confinement of persons held against their will in lawful custody or detention, especially a place where people are held for minor offenses or with reference to some future judicial proceeding. 2. Confinement in a jail. 3. The condition created by the requirement that a horse claimed in a claiming race not be run at another track for some period of time (usually 30 days).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**justice** (noun): 1. The state or characteristic of being just or fair. 2. The ideal of fairness, impartiality, etc., especially with regard to the punishment of wrongdoing. 3. Judgment and punishment of a party who has allegedly wronged another.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**class** (noun): 1. A group, collection, category or set sharing characteristics or attributes. 2. A social grouping, based on job, wealth, etc. In Britain, society is commonly split into three main classes: upper class, middle class and working class. 3. The division of society into classes.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**federal** (adjective): 1. Pertaining to a league or treaty; derived from an agreement or covenant between parties, especially between nations. 2. Pertaining to the national government level in a federal nation, as opposed to state, provincial, county, city, or town. 3. Relating to covenantalism.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**keeping** (noun): 1. Conformity or harmony. 2. Charge or care. 3. Maintenance; support; provision; feed.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**red** (noun): 1. The colour of the setting sun, blood, and strawberries; the colour which is evoked by the longest visible wavelengths (between about 625–740 nm), and a primary additive colour. 2. A revolutionary socialist or (most commonly) a Communist; a Bolshevik, a supporter of the Bolsheviks in the Russian Civil War. 3. One of the 15 red balls used in snooker, distinguished from the colours.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**sixth** (adjective): 1. The person or thing in the sixth position. 2. One of six equal parts of a whole. 3. The interval between one note and another, five notes higher in the scale; for example C to A, a major sixth, or C to A flat, a minor sixth.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**teenager** (noun): A person between thirteen and nineteen years old (inclusive).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**drop** (noun): 1. A small quantity of liquid, just large enough to hold its own rounded shape through surface tension, especially one that falls from a source of liquid. 2. A liquid medicine that is intended to be administered in drops (sense 1). 3. A very small quantity of liquid, or of anything.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**learned** (adjective): 1. Having much learning, knowledgeable, erudite; highly educated. 2. A courteous description used in various ways to refer to lawyers or judges. 3. Scholarly, exhibiting scholarship.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**lose** (verb): 1. To cease to have (something) in one's possession or capability. 2. To have (an organ) removed from one's body, especially by accident. 3. To shed (weight).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**miles** (noun): 1. A great distance in space or time. 2. much; a lot (used to emphasise a comparative)

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**ordered** (adjective): 1. In order, not messy, tidy. 2. Equipped with a partial or total order which, in any of several technical senses, respects the algebraic structure of the object (if such structure exists). See #Derived terms.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**pundit** (noun): 1. An expert in a particular field, especially as called upon to provide comment or opinion in the media; a commentator, a critic. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A learned person in India; someone with knowledge of Sanskrit, philosophy, religion and law; a Hindu scholar. 3. A native surveyor in British India, trained to carry out clandestine surveillance beyond British borders.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**reliably** (adverb): In a reliable manner.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**reaching** (verb): 1. The action of one who reaches; an attempt to grasp something by stretching. 2. Sailing on a reach, i.e. having the wind on either side and coming from an angle that is larger with respect to the bow than when sailing close-hauled.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**relegation** (noun): 1. The act of being relegated Moving from one division to a lower one, due to finishing the season with fewer points than others. 2. Moving from one division to a lower one, due to finishing the season with fewer points than others. 3. demotion in a hierarchy, for example in business

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**rayon** (noun): 1. A manufactured regenerated cellulosic fiber. 2. A ray or beam of light. 3. A circular area whose extent is measured by the length of the radius of the circle which bounds it.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**spent** (adjective): 1. Consumed, used up, exhausted, depleted. 2. Of fish: exhausted as a result of having spawned. 3. Of legislation or an enactment: no longer in force due to all of its provisions having expired or been completed.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**separate** (verb): 1. To divide (a thing) into separate parts. 2. To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect. 3. To cause (things or people) to be separate.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**step** (noun): 1. An advance or movement made from one foot to the other; a pace. 2. A rest, or one of a set of rests, for the foot in ascending or descending, as a stair, or a rung of a ladder. 3. The part of a spade, digging stick or similar tool that a digger's foot rests against and presses on when digging; an ear, a foot-rest.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**speed** (noun): 1. The state of moving quickly or the capacity for rapid motion. 2. The rate of motion or action, specifically the magnitude of the velocity; the rate distance is traversed in a given time. 3. The sensitivity to light of film, plates or sensor.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**visited** (verb): That has received a visit or visits.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**viral** (adjective): 1. Of or relating to a biological virus. 2. Caused by a virus. 3. Of the nature of an informatic virus; able to spread copies of itself to other computers.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**working** (noun): 1. Operation; action. 2. Method of operation. 3. The incidental or subsidiary calculations performed in solving an overall problem.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**zone** (noun): 1. Each of the five regions of the earth's surface into which it was divided by climatic differences, namely the torrid zone (between the tropics), two temperate zones (between the tropics and the polar circles), and two frigid zones (within the polar circles). 2. Any given region or area of the world. 3. A given area distinguished on the basis of a particular characteristic, use, restriction, etc.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**aston** (verb): 1. To astonish. 2. A lower third.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**ankle** (noun): 1. The skeletal joint which connects the foot with the leg; the uppermost portion of the foot and lowermost portion of the leg, which contain this skeletal joint. 2. To walk. 3. To cyclically angle the foot at the ankle while pedaling, to maximize the amount of work applied to the pedal during each revolution.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**built** (adjective): well-built, muscular or toned.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**consistent** (adjective): 1. Of a regularly occurring, dependable nature. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Compatible, accordant. 3. Of a set of statements: such that no contradiction logically follows from them.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**detained** (adjective): 1. Delayed or held back; kept from proceeding. 2. Held in custody or confinement.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**ends** (noun): 1. The area in close proximity to one's home; neighbourhood. 2. Money.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**education** (noun): 1. The process of imparting knowledge, skill and judgment. 2. Facts, skills and ideas that have been learned, especially through formal instruction. 3. Upbringing, rearing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**fictional** (adjective): 1. Invented, as opposed to real. 2. Containing invented elements. 3. Occurring in fiction.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**opportunity** (noun): 1. A chance for advancement, progress or profit. 2. A favorable circumstance or occasion. 3. Opportuneness.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**teen** (noun): 1. Synonym of teenager: a person between 13 and 19 years old (inclusive). 2. A black teenager or a young black person. 3. Of or having to do with teenagers; teenage

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**teenage** (adjective): 1. Of or relating to an age between thirteen and nineteen years old. 2. Brushwood for fences and hedges.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**bigger** (adjective): To make or become bigger.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**fully** (adverb): 1. In a full manner; without lack or defect; completely, entirely. 2. Used as an intensifier for a quantity. 3. Exactly, equally.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**fewer** (determiner): Less; a smaller amount of something non-integral commonly expressed as an integer

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**facility** (noun): 1. The physical means or contrivances to make something (especially a public service) possible; the required equipment, infrastructure, location etc. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. A building or campus specially designed for a specific purpose, such as incarceration, military use, or scientific experimentation. 3. The fact of being easy, or easily done; absence of difficulty; simplicity.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**girl** (noun): 1. A female child. 2. A woman, especially a young and often attractive woman. 3. A term of address to a female

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**impressive** (adjective): 1. Making, or tending to make, a positive impression; having power to impress. 2. Capable of being impressed. 3. Appealing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**importance** (noun): 1. The quality or condition of being important or worthy of note. 2. significance or prominence. 3. personal status or standing.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**king** (noun): 1. A male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy; in an absolute monarchy, the supreme ruler of his nation. 2. The monarch with the most power and authority in a monarchy, regardless of sex. 3. A male leader of a traditional Aboriginal group, often used as a title by colonists.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**knee** (noun): 1. In humans, the joint or the region of the joint in the middle part of the leg between the thigh and the shank. 2. In the horse and allied animals, the carpal joint, corresponding to the wrist in humans. 3. In birds: The tarsal joint, uniting the tarsometatarsus and the tibiotarsus (homologous to the human ankle). The joint uniting the tibiotarsus and the femur, typically hidden beneath plumage.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**kingdom** (noun): 1. A realm having a king or queen as its actual or nominal sovereign. 2. A realm, region, or conceptual space where something is dominant. 3. A rank in the classification of organisms, below domain and above phylum; a taxon at that rank (e.g. the plant kingdom, the animal kingdom).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**locked** (verb): 1. Having undergone locking; secured by a lock. 2. Protected by a mutex or other token restricting access to a resource. 3. Very drunk.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**lung** (noun): 1. A biological organ of vertebrates that controls breathing and oxygenates the blood. 2. Capacity for exercise or exertion; breath. 3. That which supplies oxygen or fresh air, such as trees, parklands, forest, etc., to a place.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**leadership** (noun): 1. The capacity of someone to lead others. 2. A group of leaders. 3. The office or status of a leader.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**lasting** (adjective): 1. Persisting for an extended period of time. 2. Persisting forever. 3. In full lasting cloth: a durable, plain woven fabric formerly used for making clothes and for the uppers of women's shoes.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**listen** (verb): 1. To use one's sense of hearing and auditory cognition in an intentional way; to make deliberate use of one's ears; to pay attention to or wait for a specific sound. 2. To accept advice or obey instruction; to agree or assent. 3. An instance of listening.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**low** (adjective): 1. Situated close to, or even below, the ground or another normal reference plane; not high or lofty. 2. Pertaining to (or, especially of a language: spoken in) in an area which is at a lesser elevation, closer to sea level (especially near the sea), than other regions. 3. Below the batter's knees.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**log** (noun): 1. The trunk of a dead tree, cleared of branches. 2. (The addition of quotations indicative of this usage is being sought:) Any bulky piece as cut from the above, used as timber, fuel etc. 3. A unit of length equivalent to 16 feet, used for measuring timber, especially the trunk of a tree.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**loss** (noun): 1. The result of no longer possessing an object, a function, or a characteristic due to external causes or misplacement. 2. The destruction or ruin of an object. 3. Something that has been destroyed or ruined.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**legendary** (adjective): 1. Of or pertaining to a legend or to legends. 2. Appearing (solely) in legends. 3. Having the splendor of a legend; fabled.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**league** (noun): 1. A group or association of cooperating members. 2. An organization of sports teams which play against one another for a championship. 3. Ellipsis of rugby league.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**longer** (adjective): One who longs or yearns for something.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**linked** (adjective): 1. Connected, either with links, or as if with links. 2. Having links (between modules, records, etc).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**maintain** (verb): 1. To keep up; to preserve; to uphold (a state, condition etc.). .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. To declare or affirm (a clause) to be true; to assert. 3. To keep in good condition and working order.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**milestone** (noun): 1. A stone milepost (or by extension in other materials), one of a series of numbered markers placed along a road at regular intervals, typically at the side of the road or in a median. 2. An important event in a person's life or career, in the history of a nation, in the life of some project, etc. 3. To place milestones along (a road, etc.).

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mechanical** (adjective): 1. Related to mechanics (the branch of physics that deals with forces acting on matter). 2. Related to mechanics (the design and construction of machines). 3. Done by machine.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**maze** (noun): 1. A labyrinth; a puzzle consisting of a complicated network of paths or passages, the aim of which is to find one's way through. 2. Something made up of many confused or conflicting elements; a tangle. 3. A confusion of thought; a state of bewilderment.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**minority** (noun): 1. The state or condition of being smaller, inferior, or subordinate to something or someone else; lesserness. 2. The state of being a minor; youth, the period of a person's life prior to reaching adulthood. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 3. Any subgroup that does not form a numerical majority.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**midterm** (adjective): 1. Halfway through a term, or roughly so. 2. A midterm school exam (i.e., halfway through the term). 3. A midterm election.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mission** (noun): 1. A set of tasks that fulfills a purpose or duty; an assignment set by an employer, or by oneself. 2. A important goal or purpose; an objective. 3. A missionary expedition.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**martin** (noun): Many of the various passerine birds of the family Hirundinidae, which also includes swallows, that catch insects whilst flying.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mbuga** (noun): 1. A heavy dark clay soil found in parts of Africa. 2. A seasonal swamp in East Africa.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**misleading** (adjective): 1. Deceptive or tending to mislead or create a false impression, even if technically true. 2. A deception that misleads.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**memorial** (noun): 1. Memory; recollection. .mw-parser-output .defdate{font-size:smaller} 2. Something, such as a monument, by which someone or something is remembered. 3. A chronicle or memoir.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mum** (noun): 1. mother 2. A chrysanthemum. 3. A decoration traditionally made of chrysanthemums and ribbons, worn by girls at high school homecoming celebrations, marked with indicators such as the wearer's name, school, the year, and so on.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**massive** (adjective): 1. Very large in size or extent. 2. Substantial in mass; bulky, heavy and solid. 3. To a very great extent; total, utter.

_Source: Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0)._

**mini** (adjective): 1. Miniature, tiny, small. 2. Abbreviation of miniskirt. 3. Abbreviation of minicomputer.
